land.text: the Nile Delta, where a provincial family broke away from the 13th Dynasty

predecessors.note: me-03-a's Middle Kingdom dossier records the loss of the Delta to this dynasty at 1700.

land.text: the Delta, which fell to the Hyksos 15th Dynasty around 1650

successors.note: me-03-b's Hyksos dossier names this dynasty as predecessor.

capitals.name: Avaris (Tell el-Dab'a)
capitals.note: Infobox "Capital: Xois or Avaris"; Manetho and Syncellus give Xois (Sakha) in the central Delta; the Second Intermediate Period page says most Egyptologists consider Avaris the seat.

correction.text: the Nile Delta, between Athribis in the west and Bubastis in the east, the territory Ryholt says the 14th Dynasty directly controlled

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; no Cliopatria row (its Middle Kingdom shape of -1700..-1601, 433,182 km2, still draws the Delta). The infobox gives no area; a 110 km radius around Avaris (about 38,000 km2) approximates the eastern and central Delta. Seals of the dynasty found in Middle and Upper Egypt, at Dongola and on the Levantine coast are trade or prestige finds, not territory.

ledger.note: 1700: a provincial family in the Nile Delta breaks away and forms the Fourteenth Dynasty. The Second Intermediate Period page dates the dynasty c. 1700–1650; the dynasty's own page gives c. 1725 (infobox) and Ryholt's c. 1805 and Bietak's c. 1720 as alternatives, with Canaanite immigrants in the East Delta who "declared their independence".

1650: the Fourteenth Dynasty falls to the Hyksos. The page says it ended "until its demise under the Hyksos 15th Dynasty around 1650 BC" after a Delta famine, possibly with plague; the last ruler is probably Apepi (Apophis I), though that is disputed.
1650: the Delta kingdom of the Fourteenth Dynasty ends; the Hyksos take its land.

wars.name: Hyksos conquest of the Delta
wars.outcome: The 14th Dynasty fell quickly to Hyksos power around 1650 and the Hyksos ruled Lower Egypt from Avaris.
wars.note: The page gives no campaign and no years; -1655 is the researcher's bracket. [Reviewer me-03-x, 2026-10-19] from moved -1655 to -1650: no page dates a campaign, and the Fourteenth Dynasty page gives only its "demise under the Hyksos 15th Dynasty around 1650 BC".

certainty.note: Ryholt gives the Delta with borders near Athribis and Bubastis; no page gives a frontier line.

sources.title: Second Intermediate Period of Egypt
sources.note: c. 1700–1650, Avaris as seat, the Hyksos at Avaris.

notes: Dates disagree widely: infobox c. 1725–1650, Second Intermediate Period page c. 1700–1650, Ryholt's c. 1805 start (a break during or after the late 12th Dynasty), Bietak's c. 1720. -1700 is used to match me-03-a's loss event (Middle Kingdom, 1700) and Hyksos found at 1650. The page places Nehesy c. 1705 and gives no reign lengths, so no ruler strip. The capital is Avaris (most Egyptologists) or Xois (Manetho); both are in the 110 km radius. The 14th Dynasty page also calls the 13th a Theban dynasty contemporary with it; the 13th is inside Cliopatria's Middle Kingdom row (me-03-a).
